observation_summary: The compiler was incorrectly optimizing 'if (f.onchange) { f.onchange(); }' into 'f.onchange && f.onchange();', which caused an 'Object doesn't support this action' error in Internet Explorer due to a specific bug in how IE handles event handler method calls when their return value is used.
reasoning_summary: The fix involves adding a conditional check to prevent the peephole optimization from triggering when the expression involves an event handler (methods starting with 'on'). This is a classic 'Checking' defect where a guard condition was missing to validate whether the optimization is safe for specific types of method calls in the target environment.
evidence_used: The fix adds a new conditional block: 'if (maybeExpr.getType() == Token.EXPR_RESULT) { ... }' and further checks 'if (calledFn.getType() == Token.GETELEM) { return false; } else if (calledFn.getType() == Token.GETPROP && calledFn.getLastChild().getString().startsWith("on")) { return false; }'.
The bug report explicitly mentions that the optimization 'e.onchange && e.onchange(...)' causes an error in IE, and the fix is to avoid this optimization for event handlers.
The fix introduces a guard to prevent the transformation, which is the definition of a 'Checking' defect.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the optimization logic is a method, the root cause is the absence of a guard condition to handle a specific edge case (IE event handler behavior), which is more precisely classified as 'Checking'.
